html:
The Latvian War of Independence was fought from 1918 to 1920 by the new Republic of Latvia against Soviet Russia and then against German forces trying to keep the Baltic under German control.

Latvia was proclaimed on 18 November 1918, in a theatre in Riga. Within weeks the Red Army took most of the country, and the government held on only at Liepāja. With German volunteers, Estonian help and British ships, it drove the Reds back. Then the Germans turned on the government, and were beaten near Riga in November 1919, still marked as Lāčplēsis Day.

Soviet Russia recognised Latvia in the peace of August 1920. A land reform then broke up the estates of the German nobles. The state lasted until the Soviet occupation of 1940, and the Latvian Riflemen fought on both sides. Compare the Estonian war.
sum: The Latvian War of Independence was fought from 1918 to 1920 by the new Republic of Latvia against Soviet Russia and then against German forces trying to keep the Baltic under German control.
